title: The first tap doesn't count
prompt: It is 10:36 ET. Read the chart and decide.

intro.beginner: Price came back toward the area an hour ago and bounced before reaching it. Look at what the bounce means for where your order should be.

whyNot.label: buying the first reaction
whyNot.why: It bounced from above the gap, never entering it. The area is where the edge was, and buying 40 points higher on a bounce is a market order that happens to look like a pullback.

whyNot.label: moving the order up to get filled
whyNot.why: A resting order that doesn't fill hasn't failed. Moving it toward price trades the location for a fill, and the stop you'd need is bigger.

reference.summary: A valid long whose first retrace tapped short of the gap and left. A limit order in the gap didn't fill and price ran. An hour in, price came back much deeper, into the gap and its order block, and then ran to the previous day high. Patience, not chasing, is the position.

bias.why: Higher highs and higher lows on the Daily and 4H; the overnight dip was a pullback.

decision.why: Keep the order where the edge is and wait. A resting limit in the gap is a valid long; passing or standing aside is defensible; chasing is the mistake.

next_objective.why: Price was drawn to the previous day high (19,566); it also traded to the unfilled gap at 19,450.5 to 19,467.25 on the way, which makes those defensible too. The question is where price was likely to be pulled, not what the next candle would do. A previous-day extreme is also a pool of buy-side or sell-side liquidity, so that answer is right on the side, if less exact.

annotations.label: 5m bullish FVG from the displacement
annotations.why: Still the entry. A first reaction above it doesn't change where the edge is.
annotations.decisionNote: Leave the order in the gap. A missed fill is not a reason to move it.

annotations.label: 5m order block under the gap
annotations.why: The alternative, and where the deeper retrace finally goes.

annotations.label: First retrace low 19,405.5
annotations.why: A bounce from above the gap: not a retest of it. Buying it is a market order in disguise.
annotations.whyNot: A reaction near an area isn't a reaction from it.

annotations.label: Overnight low 19,357.5
annotations.why: Sell-side liquidity swept at the open.

confluences.label: The origin gap is still unfilled
The first reaction from above the gap
confluences.why: A bounce that never reached the area.

trade.confirmationLabel: the displacement that closed above the last 5m high

lookFor: A resting order that hasn't filled is an order working, not an order failing.
Price coming near an area and bouncing isn't the area being tested.
